from: October book, night 7 (Written on His Hands)
p1: Once the Lord’s people felt sad and all alone. They said, “The Lord has forgotten me.”
The Lord answered with a question: “Can a mother forget her baby?” Then He said, “Even if she could, I will not forget you.”
He said He had carved them on the palms of His hands. That is the inside of your hand, where you can always see it.
p2: Latter-day prophets teach that this is about Jesus. After He died for us and rose again, His hands still had marks. Those marks show He remembers us always.
Look at your own little hand tonight. Jesus will never forget you. He remembers you always.
old: Isaiah was a prophet. A prophet is someone Heavenly Father tells things to, so he can tell the people. Isaiah said, "Sing, sky! Be happy, earth! Sing, mountains! Heavenly Father has comforted His people." Comforted means He made their sad hearts feel better. Isaiah said even the mountains should sing, because the good news was that big.

But Heavenly Father's people were far from home. Soldiers had taken them to a faraway land called Babylon, and they had been there a long, long time. Some of them felt forgotten. They said quietly, "Heavenly Father has left us. He does not remember us anymore."

So Heavenly Father asked them a gentle question. "Can a mother forget her little baby? Can she stop loving the child she holds?" He picked a mother and a baby on purpose, because that is the safest, closest love a child knows. And then He said something even bigger: "Even if a mother could forget, I will never forget you."

"Look," Heavenly Father said. "I have carved your name into the palms of My hands." Palms are the soft inside part of your hands. Long ago, when people must not forget something, they wrote it on their hand so they would see it all day. Carved means cut right in, so it can never rub off, not ever. Isaiah was telling them that the One who comforts His people would come, and He is Jesus - and Jesus has marks in His hands that will never rub off either.

Tonight, you are the one whose name is written there. Every time Heavenly Father opens His hands, He sees you. And if you see someone tomorrow who looks left out, you can go stand by them, the way Willow did not walk past the boy alone at the fence - because nobody is forgotten.
